solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soil behind Henry's house

indicators.note: behind means the soil comes after Henry, placed at the back

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
soil is earth

explanation.surface: Some dirt has been dumped at the back of Henry's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth, the fireside, stands by metonymy for the home or household itself.

clue.text: Silence surrounding old part of signal

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for silence wraps itself around the other piece

blocks.note: hist is an old call for silence, like 'hush'
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A quiet moment wrapped around an outdated piece of a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: HI(O)ST. A hoist is a group of flags run up together as a naval signal, and also the edge of a flag next to the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: In flag signalling a hoist is one set of flags raised at once, so it forms a component of a signal.

clue.text: Administrative trainee covering rent by son accepts new tenancy

indicators.note: in a down clue covering means sitting on top of, so the trainee comes first

blocks.note: AT is the abbreviation for administration trainee in the civil service
rent as the past participle of rend: torn
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A junior civil servant, besides a son, agrees to a fresh lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' reads as money paid for a tenancy, but it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: To attorn is a legal term meaning to acknowledge a new landlord and continue as tenant under them.

clue.text: Come up again in core curriculum

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the following phrase

blocks.note: the run of letters straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A topic that keeps resurfacing in the basic school syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen or appear again, the same as coming up again.

clue.text: Upsetting newspaper in habitual response that's automatic

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A disturbing tabloid becomes part of someone's reflex routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' looks like part of the wordplay's action, but it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is distressing, so it is upsetting in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Virile sort topped with unruly hair who opposes Ormuzd

indicators.note: unruly hair is out of order, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue topped with puts the second piece above the first

blocks.note: the four letters of hair, mixed up
a virile sort is a real man

explanation.surface: A macho fellow with messy hair who stands against some rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Ormuzd (Ahura Mazda) is the good god of Zoroastrianism; his evil adversary is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Zoroastrian belief Ahriman is the destructive spirit locked in eternal conflict with the good god Ormuzd.

clue.text: She does flirt with one at centre

indicators.note: with one at centre means the middle letter is swapped for a single unit

blocks.note: to dally is to flirt or trifle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman who flirts, with somebody in the middle of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: The central L of DALLY becomes I. A daily is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day: she 'does' for the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a domestic cleaner, and in British idiom such a woman 'does for' a family, hence 'she does'.

clue.text: Conceivably do true scenic route?

indicators.note: conceivably suggests one possible version of the words, a rearranged one

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the picturesque road really the right way to go?
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout way, the kind of indirect path taken for the views.

clue.text: A large island so far about to become refuge

indicators.note: about means the island and the 'so far' word are turned round

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
an ait is a small river island
as, as in 'as far as'

explanation.surface: A big island has until now been on the turn towards being a haven.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsatia was the slang name for Whitefriars in London, once a sanctuary where debtors and criminals escaped arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatia came to mean any sanctuary or asylum for lawbreakers, after the old Whitefriars precinct.

clue.text: Previously as in releasing a lenient locum?

indicators.note: releasing lets the letters loose so they can fall into a new order
in means the first piece is lodged within the scrambled letters

blocks.note: ut is the Latin for as, a language spoken formerly
eight letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: Releasing a soft-hearted stand-in, as happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: UT goes into the rearranged A LENIENT, after its third letter. The word's root is French lieu tenant, one holding a place for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a deputy acting in a superior's place, exactly what a locum is.

clue.text: Toadies succeeded splitting peninsular republic

indicators.note: splitting means one piece breaks into the middle of the other

blocks.note: Yemen sits on the Arabian peninsula
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Flatterers have managed to divide an Arabian state.
explanation.walkthrough: YE(S)MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who always agree with the boss, the same as toadies.

clue.text: Buried shellfish is perhaps Tarka's worst nightmare?

indicators.note: perhaps marks Tarka as one example standing for a whole kind of animal

blocks.note: Tarka is the otter of Henry Williamson's novel, so his is an otter's
the worst imaginable ordeal

explanation.surface: A clam hidden in mud is apparently what a famous otter dreads most.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as OTTER'S HELL. Tarka the Otter is a classic English nature novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter shell is a large bivalve mollusc that lives deeply burrowed in sand or mud.

clue.text: Means to level ground of latest against being included

indicators.note: ground, as in crushed and broken, means these letters are reshaped
being included means the next word is put inside the other letters

blocks.note: eight letters for rearranging
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A device for flattening newly broken earth, set against some inclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: ON joins the letters of OF LATEST and all ten are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A floatstone is a bricklayer's smoothing stone used to rub surfaces level, so it is a tool for levelling.

clue.text: Fresh satires? That's our dream

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the following word is made over in a new order

blocks.note: seven letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: Pretentious types longing for some new lampoons.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the answer: arty folk dreaming of new satires.
explanation.definitionFit: Artsies are people with artistic pretensions, the sort who would crave novel satirical work.

clue.text: Hound is circling round stretch of Irish water

indicators.note: round signals the little word is turned the other way
circling means going all around the next piece

blocks.note: the word is, read in the other direction
a lough is an Irish lake or sea inlet

explanation.surface: A dog swims in circles around part of an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloughi is a North African breed of sighthound, a dog related to the saluki.

clue.text: Timber, erm, material once common in joints for seafarers

definitions.text: material once common in joints for seafarers

blocks.note: oak is a timber
um, like erm, is a hesitation noise

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly naming the wood once used to seal ships' seams.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose hemp fibre once driven into the seams of wooden ships for caulking.

clue.text: Steamy gossip that's spiteful going round about privates?

indicators.note: going round means the gossip word is turned back to front
about means it then wraps around the soldiers

blocks.note: dirt is malicious gossip
OR is other ranks, the privates and NCOs of the army

explanation.surface: Racy scandal about soldiers circulates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' tempts a rude reading; it means rank-and-file soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid can mean passionate and sexually charged, the sense of steamy as in a hot romance.

clue.text: This convert expressing thanks would be silent

indicators.note: expressing means pressing out, so take the thanks word out of the answer

blocks.note: mute means silent
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A grateful convert would keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse logic: 'this' (the answer), with thanks pressed out of it, would leave the word for silent, so the answer is that word with thanks inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change form, a sense shared with convert used as a verb.

clue.text: Sugar with pot of tea

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking pot
o' is a short form of of
cha (char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Sweetener with a pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Panocha is a coarse brown Mexican sugar, and also a fudge made from brown sugar.

clue.text: Dramatic midnight? Neither this nor that, finish up with day in fact

definitions.text: Dramatic midnight? Neither this nor that

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word is flipped

blocks.note: to do is to finish, as in done for
D is the abbreviation for day
even as an intensifier: indeed, in fact

explanation.surface: A theatrical midnight that ends one day and starts another.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth the hour near midnight is 'at odds with morning, which is which'; Shakespeare's odd-even means that indeterminate time.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd-even names the moment of midnight in Shakespearean usage, a time that is neither one day nor the next.

clue.text: Noise-reducing gizmo Sikh fixed in shed

indicators.note: fixed, as in rigged, tells the solver to rearrange the letters
in places the rearranged letters inside the building

blocks.note: a hut is a shed
the letters of Sikh, mixed up

explanation.surface: A man repairs a silencer in his shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hush kit is a set of fittings added to a jet engine to make it quieter.

clue.text: Frees from French a daughter in specs

indicators.note: in puts the daughter inside the eyewear word

blocks.note: un is French for a
bins is British slang for glasses
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A French girl wearing glasses is let loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbind is to untie or release, so unbinds means frees.

clue.text: Good, since cases lead to politicians finding uppermost reserve

indicators.note: lead means only the front letter of the word before it is wanted

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
the first letter of cases
taken as an abbreviation for a party's politicians, such as the Alliance Party

explanation.surface: Good cases lead MPs to discover a top hidden stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The G, AS and C are secure; how 'to politicians' yields AP is not certain, and the Alliance Party is the best guess.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas cap is the layer of gas trapped above the oil in a reservoir, a reserve sitting on top.

clue.text: Christ, a rather uplifting case of dry eye?

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means raising from bottom to top, so read backwards

blocks.note: X, the Greek chi, stands for Christ as in Xmas
taken as written
more, as in 'more tired than ill'

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at an uplifting case of dry eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeroma is the medical term for abnormal dryness of the conjunctiva, an instance of dry eye.

clue.text: Unsafe to associate with head missing coarse material about new cases

indicators.note: head missing means the first letter is dropped
cases means holds inside, as a case holds its contents

blocks.note: gunny is coarse sacking
ca is circa, about
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A rough sack with its top missing is dodgy to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, uncanny can mean dangerous or not safe to meddle with, beyond its everyday sense of weird.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the Scots sense of uncanny as unsafe or dangerous, someone not safe to have dealings with.

clue.text: Copper seldom used muscle relaxant

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare means seldom found

explanation.surface: A policeman rarely uses a drug to loosen muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract that paralyses muscles, used in surgery to relax them.

clue.text: Attendant officer's securing special indirect efforts

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly within

blocks.note: an aide is an officer's assistant; aide's becomes the letters here
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: An adjutant is grasping some special roundabout measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks made indirectly or off to one side, here taken as oblique attempts.

clue.text: Coach then court conductor

blocks.note: a coach is a bus
the bar is the rail in court where the accused stands

explanation.surface: A bus trip followed by court for the driver or ticket collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests a bus conductor; it is an electrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A busbar is a metal strip carrying a large electric current, an electrical conductor.

clue.text: Second squad's salary

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a crew is a team or squad

explanation.surface: The pay of the reserve team.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British slang for wages, as in being on a good screw.

clue.text: Repeat opening deals similar to loans

blocks.note: a rep is a repetition, as in a gym exercise
os is the anatomical term for a mouth or opening

explanation.surface: Repeating the first few transactions resembling credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A repo is a sale-and-repurchase agreement, a financial deal that works like a secured loan.

clue.text: More sexy Gallic friend stripped off causing excitement among Scots

indicators.note: stripped off means those letters are peeled away and removed

blocks.note: steamier, racier
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A sexier French lover undresses and causes a stir in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots a steer is a commotion or stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Steer is a Scots word for a disturbance or bustle, the same as a stir of excitement.

clue.text: Central to shepherds and oddly irenic — it's how Pan is

indicators.note: central to means only the middle letter is wanted
oddly means strangely, so the letters are set out in a strange new order

blocks.note: the fifth of nine letters
the letters of irenic, mixed

explanation.surface: Peaceful shepherds describe the character of the pastoral god.
explanation.definitionFit: Hircine means goat-like, and Pan the Greek god had a goat's legs and horns.

clue.text: Arrange a meeting with Charlie about working with Victor

indicators.note: about means going round the other pieces

blocks.note: charlie is slang for cocaine, coke
on means working or operating
Victor is V in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Setting up a get-together with Charlie and Victor at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like the radio-alphabet C; it is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To convoke is to call people together formally, which is to summon a meeting.

clue.text: Cold dessert is deformed if stirred

indicators.note: stirred means mixed about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: ten letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: An iced pudding gets misshapen when you mix it.
explanation.definitionFit: Semifreddo is an Italian half-frozen dessert, like a soft ice cream or mousse.

clue.text: Write note with a feather

blocks.note: to pen is to write
N is the abbreviation for note
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jotting a message with a quill.
explanation.definitionFit: Penna is the technical term for a contour feather of a bird.

clue.text: Tips from some experts loading up sheds for modern yards

indicators.note: tips from means only the end letters of these words are wanted
loading up means those letters are added onto the end of the next piece

blocks.note: a hawk mews when it moults, so mews means sheds
the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Specialists offer advice on stacking garden huts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds' looks like a noun for garden huts; it is the verb, moults.
explanation.definitionFit: Mewses are rows of former stables converted to houses, the modern form of the stable yard.
